target_customer: Players of its multiplayer games; since 2024 game developers and publishers buying the Harbor community software
problem: Games need strong communities to grow and retain players, and developers lack tools to engage superfans across channels like Discord.
business_model: Game sales and free to play with paid add-ons (Enemy On Board, SWORN published by Team17); B2B community software (Harbor)
product_category: Multiplayer game studio and community software

founders.name: Colin Feo
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO by GamesBeat 2024-10-10; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Werewolf and Mafia style social deduction games
competitors.what: Hidden role party games, mostly word based or in person, which Enemy On Board adapted into an action game
competitors.traction_then: Established genre; no figures in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: Online multiplayer action game with netcode and a small team; Harbor later added community software.

defensibility.rationale: Game mechanics are easy to copy, and community and IP are the main protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of copying or acquisition. The company moved to publishing SWORN with Team17 and launched Harbor.

market_need_then: Social deduction games were popular as a format, and online multiplayer communities form around Discord and Steam. The source did not give specific demand data.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community focused tagline: Creating Communities Through Gaming

branding.brand_signature: Community driven studio with an active Discord (about 21,600 members in the SWORN community per Steam listing)
branding.community_and_virality: SWORN has an active Discord, Reddit and X presence; Enemy On Board has about 1,500 Steam reviews, mostly positive.

brand_strength.rationale: Studio is known for community building, with a Discord following and a Team17 publishing deal, but no brand press found beyond product launches.

pivots.to: Added Harbor, community software for game developers
pivots.why: Studio's community tools became a product; see GamesBeat 2024-10-10.

outcome_analysis: Windwalk shipped Enemy On Board to Steam early access in 2020, later co-developed SWORN with publisher Team17, and in 2024-10 raised a $4.5M seed to launch Harbor, a community growth tool claiming 5 million monthly active users across partners. It is still active with about 25 people. The studio survived by extending from games into software, though earlier funding and revenue are unknown.
notes: Funding: CB Insights gives $4.65M total, other aggregators $4.5M; round date varies between October and November 2024; ZoomInfo names a16z as lead, unconfirmed elsewhere. Earlier funding (2019 to 2023) not found. The competitor source is dated 2019-10, about seven months after the Winter 2019 batch. Founder backgrounds were not found in a source opened; search snippets suggest Colin Feo is a former game designer, not recorded. Cris Feo and Samuel Leonard are listed on the YC page; Colin Feo only in press.
